description: Table 8 is a single, fully legible raster table (no graph or micrograph panels) with four column headers: "Samples", "Aging states", "ε" (a dimensionless parameter), and "ρ [m⁻²]" (dislocation density in inverse square metres). It lists two sample groups of eight rows total. The first group, "0.02Nb steels", spans four aging states: "as-cast" (ε = 0.262, ρ = 9.69 × 10¹⁴ m⁻²), "723 K/3 h" (ε = 0.285, ρ = 1.05 × 10¹⁵ m⁻²), "773 K/3 h" (ε = 0.258, ρ = 9.55 × 10¹⁴ m⁻²) and "823 K/3 h" (ε = 0.283, ρ = 1.04 × 10¹⁵ m⁻²). The second group, "0.04Nb steels", gives "as-cast" (ε = 0.249, ρ = 1.07 × 10¹⁵ m⁻²), "723 K/3 h" (ε = 0.268, ρ = 1.15 × 10¹⁵ m⁻²), "773 K/3 h" (ε = 0.257, ρ = 1.10 × 10¹⁵ m⁻²) and "823 K/3 h" (ε = 0.265, ρ = 1.13 × 10¹⁵ m⁻²). The table reports these ε and ρ values specifically for ferrite. Across every aging state the 0.04Nb steels show higher ρ than the corresponding 0.02Nb steels, and both the as-cast and 723 K/3 h conditions carry the highest ρ within each group. The table supplies the ε and ρ inputs used with the Taylor factor M_F = 2, α_F = 0.4 and G_F = 76 GPa to compute the ferrite dislocation strengthening.

subfigures.description: Four-column table (Samples, Aging states, ε, ρ [m⁻²]) listing ε and dislocation density ρ for ferrite in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels across four aging states (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h).

observations.observation: Table 8 columns are headed 'Samples', 'Aging states', 'ε', and 'ρ [m⁻²]', reporting values for ferrite.
For 0.02Nb steels the ferrite ε values are 0.262 (as-cast), 0.285 (723 K/3 h), 0.258 (773 K/3 h) and 0.283 (823 K/3 h).
For 0.02Nb steels the ferrite ρ values are 9.69 × 10¹⁴ (as-cast), 1.05 × 10¹⁵ (723 K/3 h), 9.55 × 10¹⁴ (773 K/3 h) and 1.04 × 10¹⁵ m⁻² (823 K/3 h).
For 0.04Nb steels the ferrite ε values are 0.249 (as-cast), 0.268 (723 K/3 h), 0.257 (773 K/3 h) and 0.265 (823 K/3 h).
For 0.04Nb steels the ferrite ρ values are 1.07 × 10¹⁵ (as-cast), 1.15 × 10¹⁵ (723 K/3 h), 1.10 × 10¹⁵ (773 K/3 h) and 1.13 × 10¹⁵ m⁻² (823 K/3 h).
At every aging state the 0.04Nb steels have higher ferrite dislocation density ρ than the 0.02Nb steels.
The highest ferrite ρ in the 0.02Nb group occurs at 723 K/3 h (1.05 × 10¹⁵ m⁻²), while the lowest occurs at 773 K/3 h (9.55 × 10¹⁴ m⁻²).
The citing text states the ε and ρ values of Table 8 are used with M_F = 2, α_F = 0.4 and G_F = 76 GPa to estimate ferrite dislocation strengthening.
The citing text gives the resulting ferrite dislocation strengthening as 79.7 MPa (as-cast), 84.0, 83.5 and 93.3 MPa (aging at 723, 773 and 823 K) for 0.02Nb steels.
The citing text gives the resulting ferrite dislocation strengthening as 84.3 MPa (as-cast) and 92.2, 96.4 MPa (aging at 723 and 773 K) for 0.04Nb steels.
